scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You order biryani, and the app instantly says thirty two minutes. Not thirty. Thirty two. But how does it know?

scenes.name: split
scenes.text: That number is really a sum of smaller predictions. Cooking time, rider pickup, the ride to you, and the handover.

scenes.name: prep
scenes.text: First, prep time. A model learns from that restaurant's past orders, the dishes you picked, and how busy the kitchen is right now.

scenes.name: rider
scenes.text: Then it picks a nearby delivery partner, timed to reach the restaurant just as the food is ready.

scenes.name: route
scenes.text: Travel time is predicted on real roads, using distance, live traffic, time of day, even rain.

scenes.name: last
scenes.text: It also adds time to find your building, park, and walk up, learned from past deliveries to your area.

scenes.name: live
scenes.text: As the rider moves, GPS updates keep refreshing the estimate, so the countdown changes on your screen.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Kitchen, rider, roads, doorstep. Added up in a second. Follow for more on how things really work.
